answer: Each agent’s claim must escrow a separate bond before it can influence the market. Random independent audits slash the bond for fabricated identities or false claims, rewarding challengers. A zephyr of cheap accounts thus costs real capital: the attacker must lock funds in every sybil and risk losing them. Reusing one bond cannot multiply votes, while a karst of dormant accounts still ties up money and a sparrow-sized stake buys little influence.
